title: Answer: no account of what intelligence is, which grew by self-selection among apes

statements.text: Matter As Machine takes no position on what intelligence is. It says where cleverness came from: once apes had an instinct to change their world, a stupid change could get one killed, so apes able to think rationally and predict the outcome of their actions survived, and the instinct worked as self-selection toward cleverer apes. Neurons themselves are not clever, and new ideas come from random or pseudorandom changes, as mutations do in evolution.

sources.quote: So this instinct causes a self-selection mechanism, where apes either become extinct or become cleverer and cleverer.
